text: We’ll give you — we’ll catch up.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: The United States is scheduled to turn over responsibility for security in Afghanistan to the Afghan government in 2014.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: At that point, we will withdraw our combat troops, leave a smaller force of Americans, if I understand our policy, in Afghanistan for training purposes.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: It seems to me the key question here is: What do you do if the deadline arrives and it is obvious the Afghans are unable to handle their security?

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Do we still leave?

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: And I believe, Governor Romney, you go first?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Well, we’re going to be finished by 2014, and when I’m president, we’ll make sure we bring our troops out by the end of 2014.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The commanders and the generals there are on track to do so.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We’ve seen progress over the past several years.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The surge has been successful and the training program is proceeding apace.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: There are now a large number of Afghan Security Forces, 350,000 that are ready to step in to provide security and we’re going to be able to make that transition by the end of 2014.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: So our troops will come home at that point.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I can tell you at the same time, that we will make sure that we look at what’s happening in Pakistan, and recognize that what’s happening in Pakistan is going to have a major impact on the success in Afghanistan.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And I say that because I know a lot of people that feel like we should just brush our hands and walk away.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And I don’t mean you, Mr.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: President, but some people in the — in our nation feel that Pakistan is being nice to us, and that we should walk away fro mthem.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But Pakistan is important to the region, to the world and to us, because Pakistan has 100 nuclear warheads and they’re rushing to build a lot more.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They’ll have more than Great Britain sometime in the — in the relatively near future.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They also have the Haqqani Network and the Taliban existent within their country.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And so a Pakistan that falls apart, becomes a failed state, would be of extraordinary danger to Afghanistan and to us.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And so we’re going to have to remain helpful in encouraging Pakistan to move towards a more stable government and rebuild the relationship with us.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And that means that our aid that we provide to Pakistan is going to have to be conditioned upon certain benchmarks being met.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: So for me, I look at this as both a need to help move Pakistan in the right direction, and also to get Afghanistan to be ready, and they will be ready by the end of 2014.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Mr.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: President?

speaker: OBAMA
text: When I came into office, we were still bogged down in Iraq and Afghanistan had been drifting for a decade.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We ended the war in Iraq, refocused our attention on Afghanistan, and we did deliver a surge of troops.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That was facilitated in part because we had ended the war in Iraq.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we are now in a position where we have met many of the objectives that got us there in the first place.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Part of what had happened is we’d forgotten why we had gone.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We went because there were people who were responsible for 3,000 American deaths.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And so we decimated Al Qaida’s core leadership in the border regions between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We then started to build up Afghan forces.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we’re now in a position where we can transition out, because there’s no reason why Americans should die when Afghans are perfectly capable of defending their own country.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, that transition has to take place in a responsible fashion.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve been there a long time, and we’ve got to make sure that we and our coalition partners are pulling out responsibly and giving Afghans the capabilities that they need.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But what I think the American people recognize is after a decade of war it’s time to do some nation building here at home.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And what we can now do is free up some resources, to, for example, put Americans back to work, especially our veterans, rebuilding our roads, our bridges, our schools, making sure that, you know, our veterans are getting the care that they need when it comes to post-traumatic stress disorder and traumatic brain injury, making sure that the certifications that they need for good jobs of the future are in place.

speaker: OBAMA
text: You know, I was having lunch with some — a veteran in Minnesota who had been a medic dealing with the most extreme circumstances.

speaker: OBAMA
text: When he came home and he wanted to become a nurse, he had to start from scratch.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And what we’ve said is let’s change those certifications.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The first lady has done great work with an organization called Joining Forces putting our veterans back to work.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And as a consequence, veterans’ unemployment is actually now lower than general population.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It was higher when I came into office.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So those are the kinds of things that we can now do because we’re making that transition in Afghanistan.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Let me go to Governor Romney because you talked about Pakistan and what needs to be done there.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: General Allen, our commander in Afghanistan, says that Americans continue to die at the hands of groups who are supported by Pakistan.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: We know that Pakistan has arrested the doctor who helped us catch Obama bin Laden.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: It still provides safe haven for terrorists, yet we continue to give Pakistan billions of dollars.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Is it time for us to divorce Pakistan?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: No, it’s not time to divorce a nation on Earth that has 100 nuclear weapons and is on the way to double that at some point, a nation that has serious threats from terrorist groups within its nation, as I indicated before, the Taliban, Haqqani Network.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s a nation that’s not like — like others and it does not have a civilian leadership that is calling the shots there.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You have the ISI, their intelligence organization, is probably the most powerful of the — of three branches there.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Then you have the military and then you have the civilian government.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: This is a nation, which, if it falls apart, if it — if it becomes a failed state, there are nuclear weapons there and you’ve got — you’ve got terrorists there who could grab their — their hands onto those nuclear weapons.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: This is — this is an important part of the world for us.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Pakistan is — is technically an ally, and they’re not acting very much like an ally right now.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But we have some work to do.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And I — I don’t blame the administration for the fact that the relationship with Pakistan is strained.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We — we had to go into Pakistan.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We had to go in there to get Osama bin Laden.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That was the right thing to do.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And — and that upset them, but obviously there was a great deal of anger even before that.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But we’re going to have to work with the — with the people in Pakistan to try and help them move to a more responsible course than the one that they’re on.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And it’s important for them.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s important for the nuclear weapons.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s important for the success of Afghanistan.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Because inside Pakistan, you have a — a large group of Pashtun that are — that are Taliban.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They’re going to come rushing back in to Afghanistan when we go.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And that’s one of the reasons the Afghan Security Forces have so much work to do to be able to fight against that.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But it’s important for us to recognize that we can’t just walk away from Pakistan.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But we do need to make sure that as we — as we send support for them, that this is tied to them making progress on — on matters that would lead them to becoming a civil society.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Let — let me ask you, Governor because we know President Obama’s position on this, what is — what is your position on the use of drones?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Well I believe we should use any and all means necessary to take out people who pose a threat to us and our friends around the world.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And it’s widely reported that drones are being used in drone strikes, and I support that and entirely, and feel the president was right to up the usage of that technology, and believe that we should continue to use it, to continue to go after the people that represent a threat to this nation and to our friends.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But let me also note that as I said earlier, we’re going to have to do more than just going after leaders and — and killing bad guys, important as that is.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We’re also going to have to have a farm more effective and comprehensive strategy to help move the world away from terror and Islamic extremism.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We haven’t done that yet.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We talk a lot about these things, but you look at the — the record, you look at the record.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You look at the record of the last four years and say is Iran closer to a bomb?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Yes.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Is the Middle East in tumult?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Yes.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Is — is al-Qaida on the run, on its heels?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: No.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Is — are Israel and the Palestinians closer to reaching a peace agreement?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: No, they haven’t had talks in two years.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We have not seen the progress we need to have, and I’m convinced that with strong leadership and an effort to build a strategy based upon helping these nations reject extremism, we can see the kind of peace and prosperity the world demands.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, keep in mind our strategy wasn’t just going after bin Laden.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We created partnerships throughout the region to deal with extremism in Somalia, in Yemen, in Pakistan.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And what we’ve also done is engaged these governments in the kind of reforms that are actually going to make a difference in people’s lives day to day, to make sure that their governments aren’t corrupt, to make sure that they’re treating women with the kind of respect and dignity that every nation that succeeds has shown and to make sure that they’ve got a free market system that works.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So across the board, we are engaging them in building capacity in these countries.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we have stood on the side of democracy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: One thing I think Americans should be proud of, when Tunisians began to protest, this nation — me, my administration — stood with them earlier than just about any country.

speaker: OBAMA
text: In Egypt we stood on the side of democracy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: In Libya we stood on the side of the people.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And as a consequence, there’s no doubt that attitudes about Americans have changed.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But there are always going to be elements in these countries that potentially threaten the United States.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we want to shrink those groups and those networks and we can do that.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But we’re always also going to have to maintain vigilance when it comes to terrorist activities.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The truth, though, is that Al Qaeda is much weaker than it was when I came into office.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And they don’t have the same capacities to attack the U.

speaker: OBAMA
text: homeland and our allies as they did four years ago.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Let’s — let’s go to the next segment, because it’s a very important one.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: It is the rise of China and future challenges for America.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: I want to just begin this by asking both of you, and Mr.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: President, you — you go first this time.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: What do you believe is the greatest future threat to the national security of this country?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, I think it will continue to be terrorist networks.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We have to remain vigilant, as I just said.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But with respect to China, China is both an adversary, but also a potential partner in the international community if it’s following the rules.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So my attitude coming into office was that we are going to insist that China plays by the same rules as everybody else.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I know Americans had seen jobs being shipped overseas; businesses and workers not getting a level playing field when it came to trade.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And that’s the reason why I set up a trade task force to go after cheaters when it came to international trade.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s the reason why we have brought more cases against China for violating trade rules than the other — the previous administration had done in two terms.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we’ve won just about every case that we’ve filed, that has been decided.

speaker: OBAMA
text: In fact, just recently steelworkers in Ohio and throughout the Midwest — Pennsylvania — are in a position now to sell steel to China because we won that case.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We had a tire case in which they were flooding us with cheap domestic tires — or — or cheap Chinese tires.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we put a stop to it and as a consequence saved jobs throughout America.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I have to say that Governor Romney criticized me for being too tough in that tire case; said this wouldn’t be good for American workers and that it would be protectionist.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But I tell you, those workers don’t feel that way.

speaker: OBAMA
text: They feel as if they had finally an administration who was going to take this issue seriously.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Over the long term, in order for us to compete with China, we’ve also got to make sure, though, that we’re taking — taking care of business here at home.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If we don’t have the best education system in the world, if we don’t continue to put money into research and technology that will allow us to create great businesses here in the United States, that’s how we lose the competition.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And, unfortunately, Governor Romney’s budget and his proposals would not allow us to make those investments.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: All right.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Governor?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Well, first of all, it’s not government that makes business successful.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s not government investments that makes businesses grow and hire people.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Let me also note that the greatest threat that the world faces, the greatest national security threat is a nuclear Iran.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Let’s talk about China.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: China has an interest that’s very much like ours in one respect, and that is they want a stable world.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They don’t want war.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They don’t want to see protectionism.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They don’t want to see the world break out into — into various forms of chaos, because they have to — they have to manufacture goods and put people to work and they have about 20,000 — 20 million, rather, people coming out of the farms every year coming into the cities, needing jobs.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: So they want the economy to work and the world to be free and open.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And so we can be a partner with China.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We don’t have to be an adversary in any way, shape or form.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We can work with them, we can collaborate with them, if they’re willing to be responsible.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Now, they look at us and say, Is it a good idea to be with America?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: How strong are we going to be?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: How strong is our economy?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They look at the fact that we owe ’em a trillion dollars and owe other people $16 trillion in total, including that.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They look at our — our decision to — to cut back on our military capabilities.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: A trillion dollars.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The secretary of defense called these trillion dollars of cuts to our military devastating.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s not my term, it’s the president’s own secretary of defense called these trillion dollars of cuts to our military devastating.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s not my term, it’s the president’s own Secretary of Defense, called them devastating.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They look at America’s commitments around the world and they see what’s happening, and they say, well, OK.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Is America going to be strong?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And the answer is, yes, if I’m president, America will be very strong.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We’ll also make sure that we have trade relations with China that work for us.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ve watched year in and year out as companies have shut down and people have lost their jobs because China has not played by the same rules, in part by holding down artificially the value of their currency.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It holds down the prices of their goods.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It means our goods aren’t as competitive and we lose jobs.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That’s got to end.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They’re making some progress; they need to make more.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That’s why on day one, i will label them a currency manipulator, which allows us to apply tariffs where they’re taking jobs.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They’re stealing our intellectual property, our patents, our designs, our technology, hacking into our computers, counterfeiting our goods.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They have to understand we want to trade with them.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We want a world that’s stable.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We like free enterprise, but you got to play by the rules.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Well, Governor, let me just ask you.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: If you declare them a currency manipulator on day one, some people are — say you’re just going to start a trade war with China on day one.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Is that — isn’t there a risk that that could happen?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Well, they sell us about this much stuff every year, and we sell them about this much stuff every year.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: So it’s pretty clear who doesn’t want a trade war.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And there’s one going on right now, which we don’t know about it.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s a silent one.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And they’re winning.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We have enormous trade imbalance with China, and it’s worse this year than last year, and it’s worse last year than the year before.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And so we have to understand that we can’t just surrender and lose jobs year in and year out.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We have to say to our friend in China, look, you guys are playing aggressively.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We understand it.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But this can’t keep on going.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You can’t keep on holding down the value of your currency, stealing our intellectual property, counterfeiting our products, selling them around the world, even to the United States.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I was with one company that makes valves and — and process industries and they said, look, we were — we were having some valves coming in that — that were broken and we had to repair them under warranty and we looked them and — and they had our serial number on them.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And then we noticed that there was more than one with that same serial number.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They were counterfeit products being made overseas with the same serial number as a U.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: company, the same packaging, these were being sold into our market and around the world as if they were made by the U.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: competitor.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: This can’t go on.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I want a great relationship with China.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: China can be our partner, but — but that doesn’t mean they can just roll all over us and steal our jobs on an unfair basis.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, Governor Romney’s right, you are familiar with jobs being shipped overseas because you invested in companies that were shipping jobs overseas.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And, you know, that’s — you’re right.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I mean that’s how our free market works.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But I’ve made a different bet on American workers.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If we had taken your advice Governor Romney about our auto industry, we’d be buying cars from China instead of selling cars to China.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If we take your advice with respect to how we change our tax codes so that companies that earn profits overseas don’t pay U.

speaker: OBAMA
text: taxes compared to companies here that are paying taxes.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now that’s estimated to create 800,000 jobs, the problem is they won’t be here, they’ll be in places like China.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And if we’re not making investments in education and basic research, which is not something that the private sector is doing at a sufficient pace right now and has never done, then we will lose the in things like clean energy technology.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now with respect to what we’ve done with China already, U.

speaker: OBAMA
text: exports have doubled since I came into office, to China and actually currencies are at their most advantageous point for U.

speaker: OBAMA
text: exporters since 1993.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We absolutely have to make more progress and that’s why we’re going to keep on pressing.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And when it comes to our military and Chinese security, part of the reason that we were able to pivot to the Asia-Pacific region after having ended the war in Iraq and transitioning out of Afghanistan, is precisely because this is going to be a massive growth area in the future.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we believe China can be a partner, but we’re also sending a very clear signal that America is a Pacific power; that we are going to have a presence there.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We are working with countries in the region to make sure, for example, that ships can pass through; that commerce continues.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we’re organizing trade relations with countries other than China so that China starts feeling more pressure about meeting basic international standards.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s the kind of leadership we’ve shown in the region.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s the kind of leadership that we’ll continue to show.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I just want to take one of those points, again, attacking me as not talking about an agenda for — for getting more trade and opening up more jobs in this country.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But the president mentioned the auto industry and that somehow I would be in favor of jobs being elsewhere.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Nothing could be further from the truth.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’m a son of Detroit.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I was born in Detroit.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: My dad was head of a car company.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I like American cars.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And I would do nothing to hurt the U.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: auto industry.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: My plan to get the industry on its feet when it was in real trouble was not to start writing checks.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It was President Bush that wrote the first checks.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I disagree with that.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I said they need — these companies need to go through a managed bankruptcy.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And in that process, they can get government help and government guarantees, but they need to go through bankruptcy to get rid of excess cost and the debt burden that they’d — they’d built up.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And fortunately…

speaker: OBAMA
text: Governor Romney, that’s not what you said…

speaker: OBAMA
text: Governor Romney, you did not…

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You can take a look at the op-ed…

speaker: OBAMA
text: You did not say that you would provide government help.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I said that we would provide guarantees, and — and that was what was able to allow these companies to go through bankruptcy, to come out of bankruptcy.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Under no circumstances would I do anything other than to help this industry get on its feet.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And the idea that has been suggested that I would liquidate the industry, of course not.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Of course not.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Let’s check the record.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That’s the height of silliness…

speaker: OBAMA
text: Let — let — let’s…

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I have never said I would liquidate…

speaker: OBAM
text: …at the record.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: …I would liquidate the industry.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Governor, the people in Detroit don’t forget.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: …and — and that’s why I have the kind of commitment to ensure that our industries in this country can compete and be successful.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We in this country can — can compete successfully with anyone in the world, and we’re going to.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We’re going to have to have a president, however, that doesn’t think that somehow the government investing in — in car companies like Tesla and — and Fisker, making electric battery cars.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: This is not research, Mr President, these are the government investing in companies.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Investing in Solyndra.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: This is a company, this isn’t basic research.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I — I want to invest in research.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Research is great.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Providing funding to universities and think tanks is great.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But investing in companies?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Absolutely not.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Governor?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That’s the wrong way to go.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The fact of the matter is…

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’m still speaking.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: So I want to make sure that we make — we make America more competitive.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Yeah.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And that we do those things that make America the most attractive place in the world for entrepreneurs, innovators, businesses to grow.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But you’re investing in companies doesn’t do that.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: In fact it makes it less likely for them to come here…

speaker: OBAMA
text: Governor?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: …because the private sector’s not going to invest in a…

speaker: OBAMA
text: I’m — I’m — I’m happy.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: …company…

speaker: OBAMA
text: …to respond to you…

speaker: ROMNEY
text: …if — if you’re…

speaker: OBAMA
text: …you’ve had the floor for a while.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: …get someone else’s.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: OBAMA: The — look, I think anybody out there can check the record.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Governor Romney, you keep on trying to, you know airbrush history here.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You were very clear that you would not provide, government assistance to the U.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: auto companies, even if they went through bankruptcy.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You said that they could get it in the private marketplace.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That wasn’t true.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They would have gone through a…

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You’re wrong…

speaker: OBAMA
text: …they would have gone through a…

speaker: ROMNEY
text: …you’re wrong.

speaker: OBAMA
text: No, I am not wrong.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I am not wrong.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: People can look it up, you’re right.

speaker: OBAMA
text: People will look it up.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Good.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But more importantly it is true that in order for us to be competitive, we’re going to have to make some smart choices right now.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Cutting our education budget, that’s not a smart choice.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That will not help us compete with China.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Cutting our investments in research and technology, that’s not a smart choice.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That will not help us compete with China.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Bringing down our deficit by adding $7 trillion of tax cuts and military spending that our military is not asking for, before we even get to the debt that we currently have, that is not going to make us more competitive.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Those are the kinds of choices that the American people face right now.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Having a tax code that rewards companies that are shipping jobs overseas instead of companies that are investing here in the United States, that will not make us more competitive.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And the one thing that I’m absolutely clear about is that after a decade in which we saw drift, jobs being shipped overseas, nobody championing American workers and American businesses, we’ve now begun to make some real progress.

speaker: OBAMA
text: What we can’t do is go back to the same policies that got us into such difficulty in the first place.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why we have to move forward and not go back.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I couldn’t agree more about going forward, but I certainly don’t want to go back to the policies of the last four years.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The policies of the last four years have seen incomes in America decline every year for middle income families, now down $4,300 during your term.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Twenty-three million Americans still struggling to find a good job.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: When you came to office 32 million people on food stamps.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Today, 47 million people on food stamps.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: When you came to office, just over $10 trillion in debt, now $16 trillion in debt.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It hasn’t worked.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You said by now we’d be at 5.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: 4 percent unemployment.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We’re 9 million jobs short of that.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ve met some of those people.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ve met them in Appleton, Wisconsin.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I met a young woman in — in Philadelphia who’s coming out of — out of college, can’t find work.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ve been — Ann was with someone just the other day that was just weeping about not being able to get work.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s just a tragedy in a nation so prosperous as ours, that the last four years have been so hard.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And that’s why it’s so critical, that we make America once again the most attractive place in the world to start businesses, to build jobs, to grow the economy.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And that’s not going to happen by just hiring teachers.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Look, I love to — I love teachers, and I’m happy to have states and communities that want to hire teachers do that.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: By the way, I don’t like to have the federal government start pushing its weight deeper and deeper into our schools.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Let the states and localities do that.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I was a governor.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The federal government didn’t hire our teachers.

speaker: UNIDENTIFIED MALE
text: Governor?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But I love teachers.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But I want to get our private sector growing and I know how to do it.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: I think we all love teachers.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Gentlemen, thank you so much for a very vigorous debate.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: We have come to the end.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: It is time for closing statements, I believe you’re first, Mr.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: President.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, thank you very much, Bob, Governor Romney, and to Lynn University.

speaker: OBAMA
text: You’ve now heard three debates, months of campaigning and way too many TV commercials.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And now you’ve got a choice.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Over the last four years we’ve made real progress digging our way out of policies that gave us two prolonged wars, record deficits and the worst economic crisis since the Great Depression.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And Governor Romney wants to take us back to those policies, a foreign policy that’s wrong and reckless, economic policies that won’t create jobs, won’t reduce our deficit, but will make sure that folks at the very top don’t have to play by the same rules that you do.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I’ve got a different vision for America.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I want to build on our strengths.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I’ve put forward a plan to make sure that we’re bringing manufacturing jobs back to our shores by rewarding companies and small businesses that are investing here, not overseas.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I want to make sure we’ve got the best education system in the world.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we’re retaining our workers for the jobs of tomorrow.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I want to control our own energy by developing oil and natural gas but also the energy sources of the future.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Yes, I want to reduce our deficit by cutting spending that we don’t need but also by asking the wealthy to do a little bit more so that we can invest in things like research and technology that are the key to a 21st century economy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: As Commander in Chief, I will maintain the strongest military in the world, keep faith with our troops and go after those who would do us harm.

speaker: OBAMA
text: but after a decade of war, I think we all recognize we’ve got to do some nation building here at home, rebuilding our roads, our bridges and especially caring for our Veterans who sacrificed so much for our freedom.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we’ve been through tough times but we always bounce back because of our character, because we pull together and if I have the privilege of being your president for another four years, I promise you I will always listen to your voices.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I will fight for your families and I will work every single day to make sure that America continues to be the greatest nation on earth.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Thank you.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Governor?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Thank you.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Bob, Mr.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: President, folks at Lynn University, good to be with you.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’m optimistic about the future.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’m excited about our prospects as a nation.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I want to see peace.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I want to see growing peace in this country.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s our objective.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We have an opportunity to have real leadership.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: America’s going to have that kind of leadership and continue to promote principles of peace to make a world a safer place and make people in this country more confident that their future is secure.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I also want to make sure that we get this economy going.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And there are two very different paths the country can take.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: One is a path represented by the president, which at the end of four years would mean we’d have $20 trillion in debt heading towards Greece.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ll get us on track to a balanced budget.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The president’s path will mean continuing declining in take-home pay.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I want to make sure our take-home pay turns around and starts to grow.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The president’s path will mean continuing declining in take-home pay.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I want to make sure take-home pay turns around and starts to grow.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The president’s path means 20 million people out of work struggling for a good job.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ll get people back to work with 12 million new jobs.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’m going to make sure that we get people off of food stamps, not by cutting the program, but by getting them good jobs.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: America’s going to come back, and for that to happen, we’re going to have to have a president who can work across the aisle.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I was in a state where my legislature was 87 percent Democrat.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I learned how to get along on the other side of the aisle.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We’ve got to do that in Washington.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Washington is broken.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I know what it takes to get this country back, and will work with good Democrats and good Republicans to do that.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: This nation is the hope of the earth.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We’ve been blessed by having a nation that’s free and prosperous thanks to the contributions of the greatest generation.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They’ve held a torch for the world to see — the torch of freedom and hope and opportunity.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Now, it’s our turn to take that torch.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’m convinced we’ll do it.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We need strong leadership.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’d like to be that leader with your support.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ll work with you.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ll lead you in an open and honest way, and I ask for your vote.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’d like to be the next president of the United States to support and help this great nation and to make sure that we all together remain America as the hope of the earth.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Thank you so much.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: Gentlemen, thank you both so much.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: That brings an end to this year’s debates and we want to thank Lynn University and its students for having us.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: As I always do at the end of these debates, I leave you with the words of my mom, who said: “Go vote; it’ll make you feel big and strong.

speaker: SCHIEFFER
text: ” Good night.
